data.value: Each code works once and replaces password and authenticator. After using one, you set a new password and get new codes; the old ones stop working.

data.name: RepositoriesIntro
data.value: Repositories hold the backups of the BorgStudio app. They belong to one user, who can share them with others. The data is encrypted by the app; this server never sees its contents.

data.name: RepositoriesNeedLinux
data.value: This server runs on Windows: repositories can be managed here, but backups into them need a server on Linux (LXC, VM, Linux service or Docker).

data.name: RepositoriesEmpty
data.value: There are no repositories yet. Create one, or ask someone to share theirs with you.

data.name: RepositoriesEmptyNoCreate
data.value: No repository has been shared with you yet.

data.name: UserQuotaExceededHint
data.value: Your quota is used up: no new backups start until you free space (delete or prune archives) or an administrator raises it.

data.name: RepositoryNameHint
data.value: Letters, digits, '.', '-' and '_', e.g. "laptop". Shown as owner/name.

data.name: RepositoryQuotaHint
data.value: Upper limit for this repository; empty = no limit. borg enforces it.

data.name: RepositoryRenameWarning
data.value: Clients that use the old name have to be connected again.

data.name: RepositoryNotFound
data.value: It does not exist, is in the trash, or you have no access to it.

data.name: RepositoryAccessIntro
data.value: "Full" allows everything, including deleting and pruning archives. "Append only" allows new backups and restoring, but nothing can be deleted, which protects against ransomware. Everyone with access needs the repository's passphrase from its owner.

data.name: RepositoryShareHint
data.value: The passphrase is not shared: pass it on yourself.

data.name: RepositoryUnshareConfirm
data.value: {0} will no longer be able to use this repository.

data.name: RepositoryLeaveConfirm
data.value: You will no longer be able to use this repository.

data.name: AccessFullHint
data.value: Everything, including deleting and pruning archives.

data.name: AccessAppendOnlyHint
data.value: New backups, listing and restoring; nothing can be deleted.

data.name: RepositoryChangeOwnerIntro
data.value: Who should own {0}? The folder on the server moves along, and clients have to be connected again.

data.name: RepositoryMoveHint
data.value: The server copies the repository in the background and deletes it at the old place afterwards. Meanwhile it cannot be used.

data.name: RepositoryMoveNoTarget
data.value: There is no other writable datastore. Add one under Datastores first.

data.name: RepositoryDeleteIntro
data.value: The repository goes to the trash: nobody can use it any more, and after 7 days it is deleted for good. Until then it can be restored.

data.name: RepositoryDeleteConfirm
data.value: Move {0} to the trash? It will be deleted for good after 7 days.

data.name: TrashIntro
data.value: Deleted repositories stay here for 7 days and are then deleted for good. Repositories of deleted users land here too; an administrator can give them to someone else.

data.name: TrashPurgeConfirm
data.value: Delete {0} and all backups in it for good? This cannot be undone.

data.name: TrashEmptyConfirm
data.value: Delete all {0} repositories in the trash for good? This cannot be undone.

data.name: RestoreIntro
data.value: Who should own the repository? Under which name?

data.name: RestoreIntroOwnerDeleted
data.value: Its owner {0} was deleted: choose who gets it.

data.name: RestoreNameHint
data.value: Change it if the owner has a repository with this name by now.

data.name: DatastoresIntro
data.value: Datastores are folders that hold repositories, e.g. a second disk or a mounted NAS share. The folder must exist and the server must be allowed to write to it.

data.name: DatastoreDeleteConfirm
data.value: Remove {0} from the list? The folder stays on disk.

data.name: DatastorePathHint
data.value: Full path of an existing folder, e.g. /mnt/backup. In Docker, a mounted volume.

data.name: DatastoreReadOnlyHint
data.value: Takes no new repositories and no moves, e.g. while the disk is being replaced. Existing repositories keep working.

data.name: UserQuotaHint
data.value: Measured: above it, no new backups start; deleting to free space still works. Empty = no limit.

data.value: Your account may not create repositories.

data.name: ErrorUserQuotaExceeded
data.value: Your storage quota is used up.

data.name: ErrorQuotaInvalid

data.name: ErrorDatastoreNameInvalid
data.value: The name must have 1 to 64 characters.

data.name: ErrorDatastoreNameTaken

data.name: ErrorDatastorePathOverlaps

data.name: ErrorDatastoreNotEmpty

data.name: ErrorDatastoreLast

data.name: ErrorShareWithOwner
data.value: The owner always has full access.

data.name: ErrorRepositoryMoving

data.name: DevicesIntro
data.value: BorgStudio apps paired with your account and API tokens. They stay valid until you revoke them; "last used" shows forgotten ones. Revoking also removes their SSH keys; a backup that is running may finish.

data.name: DevicesEmpty
data.value: No app is paired and there are no API tokens yet. In the BorgStudio app, add a repository of type BorgStudio Server to pair it.

data.name: DeviceKindTokenHint
data.value: Token for scripts and other programs

data.name: DeviceRevokeConfirm
data.value: Revoke {0}? It can no longer use the server, and its SSH keys are removed. A backup that is running may finish.

data.name: TokenNameHint
data.value: What the token is for, e.g. "backup script on the NAS".

data.name: TokenCreatedIntro
data.value: Use it as "Authorization: Bearer <token>" for the interface at /api/v1. It has your rights for backing up: listing and creating repositories, registering SSH keys, statistics.

data.name: PairEnterCode
data.value: Enter the code the BorgStudio app shows.

data.name: PairQuestion
data.value: Should this BorgStudio app use the server as {0}?

data.name: PairHint
data.value: Only confirm if the app shows the same code. It can then list and create your repositories and back up to them, but not delete or share them.

data.name: PairApproved
data.value: Done. The app is paired and continues by itself; you can close this page.

data.name: SshAccessIntro
data.value: The BorgStudio app sets this up by itself. For borg without the app (scripts, borgmatic, Vorta), add an SSH key and use this address.

data.name: SshKeyAddIntro
data.value: The key gets your rights on this repository. Each key opens only one repository: use a separate key for each.

data.name: SshKeyPublicKeyHint
data.value: The content of the .pub file, e.g. ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub.

data.name: SshKeyRemoveConfirm

data.name: SshPublicAddressHint
data.value: Host or host:port, if clients reach the SSH service differently, e.g. through a forwarded port. Empty = the host name the client uses, port from the configuration.

data.name: SshStateStarting

data.name: SshStateDisabled

data.name: SshStateFailed

data.name: ErrorSshKeyInUse

data.name: ErrorNoAccessToRepository
data.value: You have no access to this repository.

data.name: ErrorPairingCodeUnknown
data.value: This code is unknown or expired. Start the pairing in the app again.

data.name: ErrorTokenNameInvalid
data.value: The name must have 1 to 100 characters.

data.name: ErrorTokenExpiryInPast
data.value: The end date must be in the future.

data.name: ErrorSshAddressInvalid

data.name: ExternalHetznerIntro
data.value: The server stores the repositories on the Storage Box and passes borg connections through, so access rights, quotas and statistics stay. Best use a sub-account of its own for BorgStudio: the repositories are folders named by their id right in its home.

data.name: ExternalSshIntro
data.value: Any SSH server with borg, e.g. a NAS or rsync.net. The server passes borg connections through. Best use an account of its own for BorgStudio: the repositories are folders named by their id right in its home.

data.name: ExternalHetznerUserHint
data.value: The (sub-)account, e.g. u123456-sub1; the server is u123456-sub1.your-storagebox.de, port 23.

data.name: ExternalSshUserHint
data.value: The account on the SSH server that holds the repositories.

data.name: ExternalHostKeyPublished
data.value: Its host key {0} is one Hetzner publishes; it is trusted.

data.name: ExternalHostKeyConfirm
data.value: Which host key is the server's?

data.name: ExternalHostKeyHint
data.value: Compare it with the server itself (ssh-keygen -lf /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key.pub). From now on any other key is refused.

data.name: ExternalBorgHint
data.value: The borg program there, e.g. borg-1.4 on a Storage Box.

data.name: ExternalPasswordHint
data.value: Used once to install the server's own key; it is not kept. Leave it empty if the key below is already installed.

data.name: ExternalPublicKeyHint
data.value: Without a password: add this line to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys of the account first.

data.name: ErrorExternalUserInvalid
data.value: This is not a valid user name (Storage Box: u123456 or u123456-sub1).

data.name: ErrorExternalHostInvalid
data.value: Enter a valid host name or address and a port between 1 and 65535.

data.name: ErrorExternalBorgInvalid
data.value: Choose a borg program (only letters, digits and . _ / + -).

data.name: ErrorExternalHostKeyNotPublished
data.value: The server's host key is none of those Hetzner publishes. Check the user name; if Hetzner changed its keys, add it as an SSH server.

data.name: ErrorExternalCheckFailed
data.value: Signing in or running borg there failed: {0}

data.name: StatsForecastNeedsDays
data.value: A forecast needs measurements from at least three days.

data.name: StatsNoHistory

data.name: StatsPerConnectionHint

data.name: StatsNoReports

data.name: SystemIntro
data.value: The load of the container or computer the server runs in: measured every minute, kept for 24 hours per minute, 30 days per hour and a year per day.

data.name: SystemUnsupported
